value.name: Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs)
value.description: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or naproxen are used to reduce inflammation around the compressed nerve root. They serve as a primary treatment to manage acute pain and decrease swelling in the cervical spine.

value.name: Physical Therapy
value.description: A structured program focuses on neck-strengthening exercises and postural correction to support the cervical spine. Physical therapists may also use manual mobilization to improve flexibility and reduce nerve irritation.

value.name: Cervical Traction
value.description: This therapy involves gently stretching the neck to increase the space between vertebrae and reduce pressure on the herniated disc. It is often used to provide immediate, temporary relief from radicular symptoms.

value.name: Neuropathic Pain Medications
value.description: Drugs like gabapentin or pregabalin are prescribed to specifically target nerve-related pain signals. These medications help stabilize nerve membranes and reduce the burning or tingling sensations associated with compression.

value.name: Ergonomic and Lifestyle Modification
value.description: Adjusting workstation setups and sleep posture helps maintain the natural curvature of the neck. Avoiding prolonged 'tech neck' and repetitive strain is essential to prevent the progression of disc herniation.

value.name: Cervical Epidural Steroid Injections
value.description: Corticosteroids are injected into the epidural space to deliver powerful anti-inflammatory effects directly to the site of nerve compression. This is typically reserved for patients who do not respond to oral medications or physical therapy.

value.name: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)
value.description: This surgical procedure removes the damaged disc through an incision in the front of the neck to decompress the nerve. The empty space is then filled with a graft to fuse the vertebrae together for stability.

value.name: Cervical Disc Arthroplasty
value.description: Also known as artificial disc replacement, this surgery replaces the herniated disc with a prosthetic joint. Unlike fusion, this method aims to preserve the natural motion of the cervical spine while relieving nerve pressure.
